=={{header|Omegese}}==
{{works with|omc|sha256 2c824805, aien-dev/omega-mv e5b32567, Linux AArch64}}
Omega has no imports, so the small output helpers (<code>emit</code> and friends) are part of the program.
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
om2
text nl "\n"
text sp " "
text minus "-"
text thead "number  binary  gray   decoded\n"
note emit writes every byte of a to stdout; a short write is retried, an error exits 1
fn emit a view uchar * to void
o = ulong 0
while lt o len a bound 4096
k = write 1 a o sub len a o
if le k 0
exit 1
end
o = add o ulong k
end
end
note emitu writes n in decimal; 20 digits hold every ulong
fn emitu n ulong to void
d = new uchar 20 0
i = ulong 20
v = n
while true bound 20
i = sub i 1
put d i uchar add rem v 10 48
v = div v 10
if eq v 0
break
end
end
emit part d i sub 20 i
end
note emitw writes n right-aligned in w columns (w at most 20; a wider number is not cut)
fn emitw n ulong w ulong to void
d = new uchar 20 32
i = ulong 20
v = n
while true bound 20
i = sub i 1
put d i uchar add rem v 10 48
v = div v 10
if eq v 0
break
end
end
if gt w sub 20 i
i = sub 20 w
end
emit part d i sub 20 i
end
note bin5 writes the low 5 bits of v, most significant first
fn bin5 v ulong to void
d = new uchar 5 48
for i ulong 5
if ne and shr v sub 4 i 1 0
put d i 49
end
end
emit d
end
note encode is n xor (n >> 1); decode undoes it by xoring in every right shift of g
fn encode n ulong to ulong
ret xor n shr n 1
end
note one xor per bit of g: a ulong has 64, so 64 shifts empty s
fn decode g ulong to ulong
n = g
s = shr g 1
while ne s 0 bound 64
n = xor n s
s = shr s 1
end
ret n
end
fn main to int
emit thead
for n ulong 32
g = encode n
emitw n 6
emit sp
emit sp
bin5 n
emit sp
emit sp
emit sp
bin5 g
emit sp
emit sp
emitw decode g 7
emit nl
end
ret 0
end
</syntaxhighlight>
